- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If model shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising forecasts) with positive sentiment, cap the next 3–5 days’ forecast at 1–2% above recent high to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops from recent peak), model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect downward trend.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (0.00–0.17), model often overestimates; apply 2–5% downward bias to 3–5 day horizon.
- If model forecast spikes sharply (e.g., >10% from prior day) with no recent negative sentiment, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day average to reduce lag bias.
